ENG.PREP.1
ENG.PREP.8
EK_ALANLAR.Süreç Bileşenleri:
PROCESS COMPONENTS FOR THE RELEVANT OUTCOMES IN ENG.PREP.1-ENG.PREP.8
L1
a) activate pre-existing knowledge and experience; b) identify relationships between prior knowledge, experience and contextual clues; c) make predictions; d) use visual elements to make rational predictions.
L2
a) identify the main topic by listening (to)/watching the content as a whole; b) recognise significant details and basic components.
L3
a) check initial predictions; b) classify key information; c) compare significant elements; d) recognise branching, linear or spiral relationships; e) make inferences and deductions; f) recognise holistic meaning; g) construct a detailed understanding; h) internalise and personalise meaning.
P1
a) recognise target pronunciation, stress and intonation in context; b) repeat target utterances accurately and naturally; c) use appropriate phonological features in pair/group interaction; d) reflect on recorded spoken production; e) evaluate feedback; f) use target phonological features accurately and naturally in communication.
R1
a) recall and activate relevant prior knowledge; b) recognise relationships between prior knowledge and textual/visual clues; c) make preliminary predictions; d) make detailed predictions from audiovisual clues.
R2
a) skim to identify general focus; b) scan for key components; c) read carefully for semantic and structural details; d) check predictions.
R3
a) classify significant elements; b) compare key elements; c) recognise spiral, causal and logical relationships; d) make meaningful inferences; e) internalise inferences appropriately.
V1
identify general and sentence-level contextual clues; locate target words; distinguish key vocabulary; infer and discuss meanings; verify meanings through peers, the teacher and/or dictionaries; and select and use the target vocabulary accurately, naturally and appropriately.
G1
examine contextual examples; identify target structures; compare examples; discover common features and formulate functional rules collaboratively; practise through meaningful contextualised activities; and produce accurate, authentic and natural spoken/written content.
W1-W4/W6
activate prior knowledge; understand the task and model; brainstorm and plan; conduct necessary preliminary research; draft and organise content; select appropriate discourse form, vocabulary and grammar; communicate the message clearly; and adapt/reorganise information for written communication.
S1-S5
relate prior listening, watching and reading to the speaking task; understand the model; identify the expected form; research, plan and organise content/materials; present clearly with appropriate vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation and body language; and reconstruct/share information in new communicative contexts.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
DIAGNOSTIC, FORMATIVE, AND PERFORMANCE-BASED ASSESSMENT
•
Listening/Watching-Comprehension: Students’ understanding of gist, specific information, details, and inferences is assessed through true/false, multiple-choice, and short-answer tasks.
•
Reading-Comprehension: Prediction, skimming, scanning, vocabulary-in-context, matching, table/chart completion, and identifying main ideas and supporting details are assessed.
•
Speaking-Expression: Pair dialogues, role-plays, quiz-show interaction, and the 40-second family podcast are evaluated through an observation checklist and/or rating scale, focusing on intelligibility, fluency, interaction, relevant vocabulary, and accurate use of reviewed structures.
•
Writing-Expression: The classroom campaign description, family email, travel blog, and time-machine paragraph are evaluated using a rubric and/or marking scheme, focusing on task fulfilment, organisation, coherence, vocabulary, grammatical accuracy, and mechanics.
•
Vocabulary and Grammaring: Completion, matching, and contextual-use tasks assess the reviewed vocabulary, grammatical items, and social language from Prep Year Themes 1-8.
•
Teacher records strengths and learning gaps to decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise before the next revision/new themes. Peer- and self-assessment with brief supportive feedback are included.

plan.KONU:
"Sub-themes: ""Comparing different school systems (local and international) and different education systems; school traditions, events, and celebration activities; national days and celebrations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for comparing different school systems (local and international):
Nouns: A schedule, a process, a curriculum, a structure, an evaluation, diversity, a scheme, a separation.
Verbs: To differ, to eliminate, to adapt, to vary, to distinguish.
Adjectives: Compulsory, distinct, diverse, comprehensive, flexible, structural, intense, broad, efficient, distinct, unequal, comparable.
Adverbs: Adequately, appropriately, consequently, considerably, critically, efficiently, extensively, primarily. Phrases for different education systems: Individual learning, critical thinking, an extracurricular activity, global citizenship, a multilingual education.
Vocabulary for comparing different education and school systems
Prepositions: Unlike.
Conjunctions: whereas, while.
Adverb: Yet.
Prepositional phrases: in comparison, compared to, contrary to.
Adverbial Phrases: on the contrary, in contrast, on the other hand.
Vocabulary for school traditions, events and celebrations
Nouns: A school badge, a competition, an award, a tradition, a parade, a debate, a contestant, opening day activities (icebreakers, orientation sessions), an educational excursion, a dance recital, a raffle, an award ceremony.
Verbs: to compete, to perform, to participate, to gather, to present, to volunteer, to host, to support, to cheer.
Adjectives: Annual, traditional, collaborative.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Present Tense with certain Verbs: (like, prefer, understand, want, need, know, mean, believe, remember, forget) vs the Present Progressive Tense: (The school wants to organize a book fair. Yet, the students are joining a sports tournament now).
-
Adverbs of Frequency (always, never, seldom, sometimes, often, etc): (The curriculum always differs from school to school).
-
''May and Might'' for Polite Requests: (May I see your passport?)
-
''Can and Could'' for Polite Requests: (Can I see the manager? Could you say it again?)
-
Articles and Quantifiers (A, an, the, zero article, one): (This international school hosts a folk dance recital every year)
-
Question Tags with the Simple Present Tense and the Present Progressive Tense: (She is organising an art exhibition, isn’t she?)
-
''Shall'' for Polite Requests: (Shall we go to the exhibition?)
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Present Tense vs the Present Progressive Tense: Contrasting what usually happens with what is happening now.
-
Different uses of the Simple Present Tense: (Newspaper Headlines: Schools close on Thursday). (Emphatic Use: I do like my school) (Imperative Use: Every Monday, you stand in line for the assembly).
-
Use of Adverbs of Frequency: Expressing how often certain activities or routines take place in schools; describing patterns in students’ participation or stress-related issues. -Use of ''May, Might, Can, Could'' for Polite Questions: Asking polite questions.
-
Use of Articles and Quantifiers (A, an, the, zero article, one): Introducing nouns and providing information about the specificity and countability of nouns.
-
Use of Question Tags with the Simple Present Tense and the Present Progressive Tense: Confirming or clarifying information.
-
Use of ''Shall'' for Polite Requests: Offering or proposing politely.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Education is the passport to the future.
Teamwork makes the dream work!
Stay curious, stay hungry for knowledge!
We have different systems, but the goal is the same.
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
-
Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme)."

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will explore the theme ''School Life and Education'' with a specific focus for comparing different school systems (both local and international), different education systems, and also school traditions, events, and celebrations. Students will research and prepare a multimedia presentation by comparing the structure, curriculum, and teaching methods of schools in their country with those in another country of their choice. They will also examine how schools around the world celebrate national days, festivals, and other events. The project will include visual aids such as posters or slides, and also a reflection on how these traditions and systems shape student experiences and learning. Finally, students will offer their own ideas for a new event or celebration that could enrich school life and develop cultural understanding. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To write about school systems and school traditions in English through a discussion activity by using target vocabulary and grammar.
Activity 1: School Systems and Events
Students write a short paragraph to compare two school systems (e.g. local and international) using words such as ''schedule, curriculum, and diversity'' and phrases such as ''unlike, in comparison, and whereas''. Next, they describe a school event they create, such as a talent show or cultural fair; they use target vocabulary such as ''organise, perform'' and descriptive words such as ''collaborative, competitive, traditional''. Students share their work with their classmates for feedback, and the teacher checks their use of language including target vocabulary and grammar and provides constructive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To describe different school systems and school traditions in English through a matching activity by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Vocabulary and Grammar Booster
Students work in a vocabulary matching game for different school systems and school traditions by working on target vocabulary and grammar. In pairs, they match vocabulary cards (e.g. schedule, curriculum, celebration, tradition) with their corresponding definitions or example sentences (e.g. ''A planned series of events or tasks for a school day'' for schedule), supported by visual aids and example contexts. Next, they will complete sentences by selecting the correct verb form to make a difference between the Simple Present (e.g. ''The teacher organises a book fair every year'') and the Present Progressive Tense (e.g. ''The students are attending a talent show now''). Throughout the activities, the teacher will observe and encourage students to read their answers aloud. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
"Sub-themes: ""Comparing different school systems (local and international) and different education systems; school traditions, events, and celebration activities; national days and celebrations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for comparing different school systems (local and international):
Nouns: A schedule, a process, a curriculum, a structure, an evaluation, diversity, a scheme, a separation.
Verbs: To differ, to eliminate, to adapt, to vary, to distinguish.
Adjectives: Compulsory, distinct, diverse, comprehensive, flexible, structural, intense, broad, efficient, distinct, unequal, comparable.
Adverbs: Adequately, appropriately, consequently, considerably, critically, efficiently, extensively, primarily. Phrases for different education systems: Individual learning, critical thinking, an extracurricular activity, global citizenship, a multilingual education.
Vocabulary for comparing different education and school systems
Prepositions: Unlike.
Conjunctions: whereas, while.
Adverb: Yet.
Prepositional phrases: in comparison, compared to, contrary to.
Adverbial Phrases: on the contrary, in contrast, on the other hand.
Vocabulary for school traditions, events and celebrations
Nouns: A school badge, a competition, an award, a tradition, a parade, a debate, a contestant, opening day activities (icebreakers, orientation sessions), an educational excursion, a dance recital, a raffle, an award ceremony.
Verbs: to compete, to perform, to participate, to gather, to present, to volunteer, to host, to support, to cheer.
Adjectives: Annual, traditional, collaborative.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Present Tense with certain Verbs: (like, prefer, understand, want, need, know, mean, believe, remember, forget) vs the Present Progressive Tense: (The school wants to organize a book fair. Yet, the students are joining a sports tournament now).
-
Adverbs of Frequency (always, never, seldom, sometimes, often, etc): (The curriculum always differs from school to school).
-
''May and Might'' for Polite Requests: (May I see your passport?)
-
''Can and Could'' for Polite Requests: (Can I see the manager? Could you say it again?)
-
Articles and Quantifiers (A, an, the, zero article, one): (This international school hosts a folk dance recital every year)
-
Question Tags with the Simple Present Tense and the Present Progressive Tense: (She is organising an art exhibition, isn’t she?)
-
''Shall'' for Polite Requests: (Shall we go to the exhibition?)
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Present Tense vs the Present Progressive Tense: Contrasting what usually happens with what is happening now.
-
Different uses of the Simple Present Tense: (Newspaper Headlines: Schools close on Thursday). (Emphatic Use: I do like my school) (Imperative Use: Every Monday, you stand in line for the assembly).
-
Use of Adverbs of Frequency: Expressing how often certain activities or routines take place in schools; describing patterns in students’ participation or stress-related issues. -Use of ''May, Might, Can, Could'' for Polite Questions: Asking polite questions.
-
Use of Articles and Quantifiers (A, an, the, zero article, one): Introducing nouns and providing information about the specificity and countability of nouns.
-
Use of Question Tags with the Simple Present Tense and the Present Progressive Tense: Confirming or clarifying information.
-
Use of ''Shall'' for Polite Requests: Offering or proposing politely.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Education is the passport to the future.
Teamwork makes the dream work!
Stay curious, stay hungry for knowledge!
We have different systems, but the goal is the same.
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
-
Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme)."

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will explore the theme ''School Life and Education'' with a specific focus for comparing different school systems (both local and international), different education systems, and also school traditions, events, and celebrations. Students will research and prepare a multimedia presentation by comparing the structure, curriculum, and teaching methods of schools in their country with those in another country of their choice. They will also examine how schools around the world celebrate national days, festivals, and other events. The project will include visual aids such as posters or slides, and also a reflection on how these traditions and systems shape student experiences and learning. Finally, students will offer their own ideas for a new event or celebration that could enrich school life and develop cultural understanding. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To write about school systems and school traditions in English through a discussion activity by using target vocabulary and grammar.
Activity 1: School Systems and Events
Students write a short paragraph to compare two school systems (e.g. local and international) using words such as ''schedule, curriculum, and diversity'' and phrases such as ''unlike, in comparison, and whereas''. Next, they describe a school event they create, such as a talent show or cultural fair; they use target vocabulary such as ''organise, perform'' and descriptive words such as ''collaborative, competitive, traditional''. Students share their work with their classmates for feedback, and the teacher checks their use of language including target vocabulary and grammar and provides constructive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To describe different school systems and school traditions in English through a matching activity by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Vocabulary and Grammar Booster
Students work in a vocabulary matching game for different school systems and school traditions by working on target vocabulary and grammar. In pairs, they match vocabulary cards (e.g. schedule, curriculum, celebration, tradition) with their corresponding definitions or example sentences (e.g. ''A planned series of events or tasks for a school day'' for schedule), supported by visual aids and example contexts. Next, they will complete sentences by selecting the correct verb form to make a difference between the Simple Present (e.g. ''The teacher organises a book fair every year'') and the Present Progressive Tense (e.g. ''The students are attending a talent show now''). Throughout the activities, the teacher will observe and encourage students to read their answers aloud. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
"Sub-themes: ""Comparing different school systems (local and international) and different education systems; school traditions, events, and celebration activities; national days and celebrations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for comparing different school systems (local and international):
Nouns: A schedule, a process, a curriculum, a structure, an evaluation, diversity, a scheme, a separation.
Verbs: To differ, to eliminate, to adapt, to vary, to distinguish.
Adjectives: Compulsory, distinct, diverse, comprehensive, flexible, structural, intense, broad, efficient, distinct, unequal, comparable.
Adverbs: Adequately, appropriately, consequently, considerably, critically, efficiently, extensively, primarily. Phrases for different education systems: Individual learning, critical thinking, an extracurricular activity, global citizenship, a multilingual education.
Vocabulary for comparing different education and school systems
Prepositions: Unlike.
Conjunctions: whereas, while.
Adverb: Yet.
Prepositional phrases: in comparison, compared to, contrary to.
Adverbial Phrases: on the contrary, in contrast, on the other hand.
Vocabulary for school traditions, events and celebrations
Nouns: A school badge, a competition, an award, a tradition, a parade, a debate, a contestant, opening day activities (icebreakers, orientation sessions), an educational excursion, a dance recital, a raffle, an award ceremony.
Verbs: to compete, to perform, to participate, to gather, to present, to volunteer, to host, to support, to cheer.
Adjectives: Annual, traditional, collaborative.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Present Tense with certain Verbs: (like, prefer, understand, want, need, know, mean, believe, remember, forget) vs the Present Progressive Tense: (The school wants to organize a book fair. Yet, the students are joining a sports tournament now).
-
Adverbs of Frequency (always, never, seldom, sometimes, often, etc): (The curriculum always differs from school to school).
-
''May and Might'' for Polite Requests: (May I see your passport?)
-
''Can and Could'' for Polite Requests: (Can I see the manager? Could you say it again?)
-
Articles and Quantifiers (A, an, the, zero article, one): (This international school hosts a folk dance recital every year)
-
Question Tags with the Simple Present Tense and the Present Progressive Tense: (She is organising an art exhibition, isn’t she?)
-
''Shall'' for Polite Requests: (Shall we go to the exhibition?)
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Present Tense vs the Present Progressive Tense: Contrasting what usually happens with what is happening now.
-
Different uses of the Simple Present Tense: (Newspaper Headlines: Schools close on Thursday). (Emphatic Use: I do like my school) (Imperative Use: Every Monday, you stand in line for the assembly).
-
Use of Adverbs of Frequency: Expressing how often certain activities or routines take place in schools; describing patterns in students’ participation or stress-related issues. -Use of ''May, Might, Can, Could'' for Polite Questions: Asking polite questions.
-
Use of Articles and Quantifiers (A, an, the, zero article, one): Introducing nouns and providing information about the specificity and countability of nouns.
-
Use of Question Tags with the Simple Present Tense and the Present Progressive Tense: Confirming or clarifying information.
-
Use of ''Shall'' for Polite Requests: Offering or proposing politely.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Education is the passport to the future.
Teamwork makes the dream work!
Stay curious, stay hungry for knowledge!
We have different systems, but the goal is the same.
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
-
Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme)."

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will explore the theme ''School Life and Education'' with a specific focus for comparing different school systems (both local and international), different education systems, and also school traditions, events, and celebrations. Students will research and prepare a multimedia presentation by comparing the structure, curriculum, and teaching methods of schools in their country with those in another country of their choice. They will also examine how schools around the world celebrate national days, festivals, and other events. The project will include visual aids such as posters or slides, and also a reflection on how these traditions and systems shape student experiences and learning. Finally, students will offer their own ideas for a new event or celebration that could enrich school life and develop cultural understanding. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To write about school systems and school traditions in English through a discussion activity by using target vocabulary and grammar.
Activity 1: School Systems and Events
Students write a short paragraph to compare two school systems (e.g. local and international) using words such as ''schedule, curriculum, and diversity'' and phrases such as ''unlike, in comparison, and whereas''. Next, they describe a school event they create, such as a talent show or cultural fair; they use target vocabulary such as ''organise, perform'' and descriptive words such as ''collaborative, competitive, traditional''. Students share their work with their classmates for feedback, and the teacher checks their use of language including target vocabulary and grammar and provides constructive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To describe different school systems and school traditions in English through a matching activity by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Vocabulary and Grammar Booster
Students work in a vocabulary matching game for different school systems and school traditions by working on target vocabulary and grammar. In pairs, they match vocabulary cards (e.g. schedule, curriculum, celebration, tradition) with their corresponding definitions or example sentences (e.g. ''A planned series of events or tasks for a school day'' for schedule), supported by visual aids and example contexts. Next, they will complete sentences by selecting the correct verb form to make a difference between the Simple Present (e.g. ''The teacher organises a book fair every year'') and the Present Progressive Tense (e.g. ''The students are attending a talent show now''). Throughout the activities, the teacher will observe and encourage students to read their answers aloud. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for comparing different school systems (local and international):
Nouns: A schedule, a process, a curriculum, a structure, an evaluation, diversity, a scheme, a separation.
Verbs: To differ, to eliminate, to adapt, to vary, to distinguish.
Adjectives: Compulsory, distinct, diverse, comprehensive, flexible, structural, intense, broad, efficient, distinct, unequal, comparable.
Adverbs: Adequately, appropriately, consequently, considerably, critically, efficiently, extensively, primarily. Phrases for different education systems: Individual learning, critical thinking, an extracurricular activity, global citizenship, a multilingual education.
Vocabulary for comparing different education and school systems
Prepositions: Unlike.
Conjunctions: whereas, while.
Adverb: Yet.
Prepositional phrases: in comparison, compared to, contrary to.
Adverbial Phrases: on the contrary, in contrast, on the other hand.
Vocabulary for school traditions, events and celebrations
Nouns: A school badge, a competition, an award, a tradition, a parade, a debate, a contestant, opening day activities (icebreakers, orientation sessions), an educational excursion, a dance recital, a raffle, an award ceremony.
Verbs: to compete, to perform, to participate, to gather, to present, to volunteer, to host, to support, to cheer.
Adjectives: Annual, traditional, collaborative.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)

Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Present Tense with certain Verbs: (like, prefer, understand, want, need, know, mean, believe, remember, forget) vs the Present Progressive Tense: (The school wants to organize a book fair. Yet, the students are joining a sports tournament now).
-
Adverbs of Frequency (always, never, seldom, sometimes, often, etc): (The curriculum always differs from school to school).
-
''May and Might'' for Polite Requests: (May I see your passport?)
-
''Can and Could'' for Polite Requests: (Can I see the manager? Could you say it again?)
-
Articles and Quantifiers (A, an, the, zero article, one): (This international school hosts a folk dance recital every year)
-
Question Tags with the Simple Present Tense and the Present Progressive Tense: (She is organising an art exhibition, isn’t she?)
-
''Shall'' for Polite Requests: (Shall we go to the exhibition?)
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Present Tense vs the Present Progressive Tense: Contrasting what usually happens with what is happening now.
-
Different uses of the Simple Present Tense: (Newspaper Headlines: Schools close on Thursday). (Emphatic Use: I do like my school) (Imperative Use: Every Monday, you stand in line for the assembly).
-
Use of Adverbs of Frequency: Expressing how often certain activities or routines take place in schools; describing patterns in students’ participation or stress-related issues. -Use of ''May, Might, Can, Could'' for Polite Questions: Asking polite questions.
-
Use of Articles and Quantifiers (A, an, the, zero article, one): Introducing nouns and providing information about the specificity and countability of nouns.
-
Use of Question Tags with the Simple Present Tense and the Present Progressive Tense: Confirming or clarifying information.
-
Use of ''Shall'' for Polite Requests: Offering or proposing politely.

We have different systems, but the goal is the same.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will explore the theme ''School Life and Education'' with a specific focus for comparing different school systems (both local and international), different education systems, and also school traditions, events, and celebrations. Students will research and prepare a multimedia presentation by comparing the structure, curriculum, and teaching methods of schools in their country with those in another country of their choice. They will also examine how schools around the world celebrate national days, festivals, and other events. The project will include visual aids such as posters or slides, and also a reflection on how these traditions and systems shape student experiences and learning. Finally, students will offer their own ideas for a new event or celebration that could enrich school life and develop cultural understanding. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will focus on the theme ''classroom life and learning'' by reflecting on their favourite school subjects, learning activities, study tools and innovations. They will write a personalised project in which they design their ideal classroom environment by adding their preferred subjects, activities, and tools. Students will explain why these elements make learning enjoyable or effective for them, and they will suggest improvements for their least favourite aspects. The project can be presented as a written report, a creative poster, or a short video. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To write about school systems and school traditions in English through a discussion activity by using target vocabulary and grammar.
Activity 1: School Systems and Events
Students write a short paragraph to compare two school systems (e.g. local and international) using words such as ''schedule, curriculum, and diversity'' and phrases such as ''unlike, in comparison, and whereas''. Next, they describe a school event they create, such as a talent show or cultural fair; they use target vocabulary such as ''organise, perform'' and descriptive words such as ''collaborative, competitive, traditional''. Students share their work with their classmates for feedback, and the teacher checks their use of language including target vocabulary and grammar and provides constructive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To describe different school systems and school traditions in English through a matching activity by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Vocabulary and Grammar Booster
Students work in a vocabulary matching game for different school systems and school traditions by working on target vocabulary and grammar. In pairs, they match vocabulary cards (e.g. schedule, curriculum, celebration, tradition) with their corresponding definitions or example sentences (e.g. ''A planned series of events or tasks for a school day'' for schedule), supported by visual aids and example contexts. Next, they will complete sentences by selecting the correct verb form to make a difference between the Simple Present (e.g. ''The teacher organises a book fair every year'') and the Present Progressive Tense (e.g. ''The students are attending a talent show now''). Throughout the activities, the teacher will observe and encourage students to read their answers aloud. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Objective: To talk about their favourite school subjects and learning activities in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Survey Challenge
Students work in groups to write five survey questions about classroom preferences. They keep their questions secret and submit them to the teacher for approval. Once approved, each group conducts the survey with classmates and organises the results. Groups then present their findings to the class by highlighting trends and insights (e.g. ''Most students enjoy debates because they are engaging while writing essays is the least favourite due to boredom''). After all presentations, the class votes for the group with the most effective questions and realistic results. During presentations, the teacher gives feedback on language use, clarity, and presentation skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Objective: To talk about their favourite school subjects and learning activities in English through a matching and fill-in-the-blanks activity by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Ask and Share Preferences
Students work in pairs. Students ask and answer questions in turns about their preferences on favourite school subjects and learning activities such as ''Do you like science experiments?'' or ''Which do you prefer: group discussions or silent reading?'' using responses such as ''Yes, I do!'' or ''I like group discussions better''. Next, each student presents their peer's preferences to the class, e.g. ''My friend likes science experiments and prefers group discussions''. At the end of the activity, the teacher checks the answers with the class, explains the correct options, and gives constructive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

Sub-themes: "Favourite school subjects, learning activities, study tools and innovations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for favourite school subjects and learning activities: Nouns: Passion, curiosity, satisfaction, confidence, inspiration, success, motivation. Verbs: To activate, to appreciate, to look forward to, to discover, to succeed in, to grasp. Adjectives: Engaging, inspiring, rewarding, satisfying, passionate, practical, educational, productive. Nouns: Frustration, boredom, confusion, tension, anxiety, struggle, failure, reluctance, avoidance, exhaustion, demotivation.
Verbs: To avoid, to ignore, to complain, to tolerate, to skip, to lose interest, to give up.
Adjectives: Confusing, frustrating, exhausting, irrelevant.
Vocabulary for favourite learning activities
Nouns: A debate, a presentation, a group discussion, a brainstorming session, art and craft, a quiz competition, storytelling, creating a model, field research, memorization, a repetition practice, doing a drill, silent reading, note-taking.
Vocabulary for favourite study tools and innovations
Adjectives: Efficient, user-friendly, accessible, out of date, complicated, inconvenient, old-fashioned.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Present Tense for the Future: (The presentation starts in ten minutes).
-
The Present Progressive Tense for the Future: (I am writing an essay tonight).
-
The Present Progressive Tense with Always: (He is always postponing his duties).
-
Question Tags for Related Tenses: (He is always complaining about field research, isn’t he?)
-
Making Adverbs from Adjectives (Regular and Irregular): They are quick runners. They run quickly).
-
Adjectives with -ed vs -ing: (Group discussions are complicated).
-
Correlative Conjunctions (either, neither): (She isn’t attending a group discussion next week, either).
-
Elliptical Responses (So do I, I hope so, etc.): (She likes brainstorming sessions. So do I).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Present Tense for the Future: Describing scheduled future events fixed with timetables or plans.
-
Use of the Present Progressive Tense for the Future: Describing planned future actions that are already arranged or decided.
-
Use of the Present Progressive Tense with always: Describing actions that cause irritation.
-
Use of Adverbs Made from Adjectives: Describing where, how, when, to what extent some things happen.
-
Use of Question Tags for Related Tenses: Confirming or clarifying information.
-
Use of Adjectives with -ed vs -ing: Describing the thing or situation that causes the feeling.
-
Use of Correlative Conjunctions (either, neither): Describing two alternatives or a negative choice between two alternatives.
-
Use of Elliptical Responses (So do I, I hope so, etc.): Giving brief answers in a conversation to avoid unnecessary repetition.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Mistakes are proof you’re trying!
Ask questions, grow smarter!
This class is our learning playground!
I meant to do it, but I totally spaced out.
Let’s ask the teacher, just in case.
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
-
Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will focus on the theme ''classroom life and learning'' by reflecting on their favourite school subjects, learning activities, study tools and innovations. They will write a personalised project in which they design their ideal classroom environment by adding their preferred subjects, activities, and tools. Students will explain why these elements make learning enjoyable or effective for them, and they will suggest improvements for their least favourite aspects. The project can be presented as a written report, a creative poster, or a short video. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To talk about their favourite school subjects and learning activities in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Survey Challenge
Students work in groups to write five survey questions about classroom preferences. They keep their questions secret and submit them to the teacher for approval. Once approved, each group conducts the survey with classmates and organises the results. Groups then present their findings to the class by highlighting trends and insights (e.g. ''Most students enjoy debates because they are engaging while writing essays is the least favourite due to boredom''). After all presentations, the class votes for the group with the most effective questions and realistic results. During presentations, the teacher gives feedback on language use, clarity, and presentation skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about their favourite school subjects and learning activities in English through a matching and fill-in-the-blanks activity by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Ask and Share Preferences
Students work in pairs. Students ask and answer questions in turns about their preferences on favourite school subjects and learning activities such as ''Do you like science experiments?'' or ''Which do you prefer: group discussions or silent reading?'' using responses such as ''Yes, I do!'' or ''I like group discussions better''. Next, each student presents their peer's preferences to the class, e.g. ''My friend likes science experiments and prefers group discussions''. At the end of the activity, the teacher checks the answers with the class, explains the correct options, and gives constructive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Favourite school subjects, learning activities, study tools and innovations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for favourite school subjects and learning activities: Nouns: Passion, curiosity, satisfaction, confidence, inspiration, success, motivation. Verbs: To activate, to appreciate, to look forward to, to discover, to succeed in, to grasp. Adjectives: Engaging, inspiring, rewarding, satisfying, passionate, practical, educational, productive. Nouns: Frustration, boredom, confusion, tension, anxiety, struggle, failure, reluctance, avoidance, exhaustion, demotivation.
Verbs: To avoid, to ignore, to complain, to tolerate, to skip, to lose interest, to give up.
Adjectives: Confusing, frustrating, exhausting, irrelevant.
Vocabulary for favourite learning activities
Nouns: A debate, a presentation, a group discussion, a brainstorming session, art and craft, a quiz competition, storytelling, creating a model, field research, memorization, a repetition practice, doing a drill, silent reading, note-taking.
Vocabulary for favourite study tools and innovations
Adjectives: Efficient, user-friendly, accessible, out of date, complicated, inconvenient, old-fashioned.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Present Tense for the Future: (The presentation starts in ten minutes).
-
The Present Progressive Tense for the Future: (I am writing an essay tonight).
-
The Present Progressive Tense with Always: (He is always postponing his duties).
-
Question Tags for Related Tenses: (He is always complaining about field research, isn’t he?)
-
Making Adverbs from Adjectives (Regular and Irregular): They are quick runners. They run quickly).
-
Adjectives with -ed vs -ing: (Group discussions are complicated).
-
Correlative Conjunctions (either, neither): (She isn’t attending a group discussion next week, either).
-
Elliptical Responses (So do I, I hope so, etc.): (She likes brainstorming sessions. So do I).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Present Tense for the Future: Describing scheduled future events fixed with timetables or plans.
-
Use of the Present Progressive Tense for the Future: Describing planned future actions that are already arranged or decided.
-
Use of the Present Progressive Tense with always: Describing actions that cause irritation.
-
Use of Adverbs Made from Adjectives: Describing where, how, when, to what extent some things happen.
-
Use of Question Tags for Related Tenses: Confirming or clarifying information.
-
Use of Adjectives with -ed vs -ing: Describing the thing or situation that causes the feeling.
-
Use of Correlative Conjunctions (either, neither): Describing two alternatives or a negative choice between two alternatives.
-
Use of Elliptical Responses (So do I, I hope so, etc.): Giving brief answers in a conversation to avoid unnecessary repetition.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Mistakes are proof you’re trying!
Ask questions, grow smarter!
This class is our learning playground!
I meant to do it, but I totally spaced out.
Let’s ask the teacher, just in case.
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
-
Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will focus on the theme ''classroom life and learning'' by reflecting on their favourite school subjects, learning activities, study tools and innovations. They will write a personalised project in which they design their ideal classroom environment by adding their preferred subjects, activities, and tools. Students will explain why these elements make learning enjoyable or effective for them, and they will suggest improvements for their least favourite aspects. The project can be presented as a written report, a creative poster, or a short video. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To talk about their favourite school subjects and learning activities in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Survey Challenge
Students work in groups to write five survey questions about classroom preferences. They keep their questions secret and submit them to the teacher for approval. Once approved, each group conducts the survey with classmates and organises the results. Groups then present their findings to the class by highlighting trends and insights (e.g. ''Most students enjoy debates because they are engaging while writing essays is the least favourite due to boredom''). After all presentations, the class votes for the group with the most effective questions and realistic results. During presentations, the teacher gives feedback on language use, clarity, and presentation skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about their favourite school subjects and learning activities in English through a matching and fill-in-the-blanks activity by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Ask and Share Preferences
Students work in pairs. Students ask and answer questions in turns about their preferences on favourite school subjects and learning activities such as ''Do you like science experiments?'' or ''Which do you prefer: group discussions or silent reading?'' using responses such as ''Yes, I do!'' or ''I like group discussions better''. Next, each student presents their peer's preferences to the class, e.g. ''My friend likes science experiments and prefers group discussions''. At the end of the activity, the teacher checks the answers with the class, explains the correct options, and gives constructive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Favourite school subjects, learning activities, study tools and innovations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for favourite school subjects and learning activities: Nouns: Passion, curiosity, satisfaction, confidence, inspiration, success, motivation. Verbs: To activate, to appreciate, to look forward to, to discover, to succeed in, to grasp. Adjectives: Engaging, inspiring, rewarding, satisfying, passionate, practical, educational, productive. Nouns: Frustration, boredom, confusion, tension, anxiety, struggle, failure, reluctance, avoidance, exhaustion, demotivation.
Verbs: To avoid, to ignore, to complain, to tolerate, to skip, to lose interest, to give up.
Adjectives: Confusing, frustrating, exhausting, irrelevant.
Vocabulary for favourite learning activities
Nouns: A debate, a presentation, a group discussion, a brainstorming session, art and craft, a quiz competition, storytelling, creating a model, field research, memorization, a repetition practice, doing a drill, silent reading, note-taking.
Vocabulary for favourite study tools and innovations
Adjectives: Efficient, user-friendly, accessible, out of date, complicated, inconvenient, old-fashioned.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Present Tense for the Future: (The presentation starts in ten minutes).
-
The Present Progressive Tense for the Future: (I am writing an essay tonight).
-
The Present Progressive Tense with Always: (He is always postponing his duties).
-
Question Tags for Related Tenses: (He is always complaining about field research, isn’t he?)
-
Making Adverbs from Adjectives (Regular and Irregular): They are quick runners. They run quickly).
-
Adjectives with -ed vs -ing: (Group discussions are complicated).
-
Correlative Conjunctions (either, neither): (She isn’t attending a group discussion next week, either).
-
Elliptical Responses (So do I, I hope so, etc.): (She likes brainstorming sessions. So do I).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Present Tense for the Future: Describing scheduled future events fixed with timetables or plans.
-
Use of the Present Progressive Tense for the Future: Describing planned future actions that are already arranged or decided.
-
Use of the Present Progressive Tense with always: Describing actions that cause irritation.
-
Use of Adverbs Made from Adjectives: Describing where, how, when, to what extent some things happen.
-
Use of Question Tags for Related Tenses: Confirming or clarifying information.
-
Use of Adjectives with -ed vs -ing: Describing the thing or situation that causes the feeling.
-
Use of Correlative Conjunctions (either, neither): Describing two alternatives or a negative choice between two alternatives.
-
Use of Elliptical Responses (So do I, I hope so, etc.): Giving brief answers in a conversation to avoid unnecessary repetition.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Mistakes are proof you’re trying!
Ask questions, grow smarter!
This class is our learning playground!
I meant to do it, but I totally spaced out.
Let’s ask the teacher, just in case.
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
-
Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will focus on the theme ''classroom life and learning'' by reflecting on their favourite school subjects, learning activities, study tools and innovations. They will write a personalised project in which they design their ideal classroom environment by adding their preferred subjects, activities, and tools. Students will explain why these elements make learning enjoyable or effective for them, and they will suggest improvements for their least favourite aspects. The project can be presented as a written report, a creative poster, or a short video. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To talk about their favourite school subjects and learning activities in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Survey Challenge
Students work in groups to write five survey questions about classroom preferences. They keep their questions secret and submit them to the teacher for approval. Once approved, each group conducts the survey with classmates and organises the results. Groups then present their findings to the class by highlighting trends and insights (e.g. ''Most students enjoy debates because they are engaging while writing essays is the least favourite due to boredom''). After all presentations, the class votes for the group with the most effective questions and realistic results. During presentations, the teacher gives feedback on language use, clarity, and presentation skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about their favourite school subjects and learning activities in English through a matching and fill-in-the-blanks activity by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Ask and Share Preferences
Students work in pairs. Students ask and answer questions in turns about their preferences on favourite school subjects and learning activities such as ''Do you like science experiments?'' or ''Which do you prefer: group discussions or silent reading?'' using responses such as ''Yes, I do!'' or ''I like group discussions better''. Next, each student presents their peer's preferences to the class, e.g. ''My friend likes science experiments and prefers group discussions''. At the end of the activity, the teacher checks the answers with the class, explains the correct options, and gives constructive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Physical health (body and illnesses); personal well-being with mental and emotional health; personal well-being with social health''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for personal well-being with physical health (body and illnesses):
Nouns: A lung, a joint, a heel, a consultant, healthcare, herb, hunger, a pill, recovery, a surgeon, survival, a first-aid kit, a bacterium, a cell, a mineral, relief, a surgery, a vitamin, a fever, a stroke, a cancer, a wound, an injury, anxiety, depression, an addiction, a recovery, a disability, panic, medication, an infection, a symptom, a treatment.
Verbs: To breathe, to consult, to heal, to cure, to suffer, to swallow, to operate, to bother.
Adjectives: Balanced, adequate, disabled, relieved, short-term, urgent, conscious, longterm, severe, unconscious.
Adverbs: Terribly, accidentally, adequately, appropriately, instantly, severely, strictly.
Vocabulary for personal well-being with mental and emotional health: Nouns: Mental health, psychological health, social bond/involvement, family tie, confidence, fulfilment, balance, self-awareness, empathy.
Vocabulary for practices and actions with mental and emotional health: Nouns: Mindfulness, therapy, breathing exercises, relaxation, rehabilitation.
Vocabulary for personal well-being with social health: Nouns: Loneliness, isolation, alienation, social anxiety, conflict, relief, pride, confusion, disappointment, trust, adaptation, acceptance.
Verbs: To interact, to socialise, to participate, to maintain, to contribute, to volunteer, to strengthen, to support.
Vocabulary for social relationship: Nouns: An acquaintance, a colleague, a community member, a mentor.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Past Tense versus the Past Progressive Tense: (She was suffering from a headache when her friend called her yesterday).
-
Could for Ability: (I could exercise for 30 minutes without interruption when I was younger).
-
Used to: (He used to socialise for his well-being).
-
Would: (When I was a kid, we would visit my grandparents every summer holiday).
-
Wh- questions (How long, etc.): (How long did your friend suffer from depression?).
-
Question Tags with Related Tenses: (She healed after the surgery, didn’t she?)
-
Prepositions: (among, until, on, at, in, in case, by, of, with, about, to, for, from, out of): (The consultant helped him cope with his depression).
-
Prepositional Phrases with in, for, to, at, about, with, from, of, etc.: (She struggled with frustration after the teacher announced the exam results).
-
Either, Neither, So do I, I hope so: (She can either take a short walk or do some breathing exercises to feel better). (Neither stress nor overthinking is good for your mental wellbeing). (I believe taking time for ourselves is important. So do I).(Doctors say regular exercise improves our health. I hope so!).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Past Tense versus the Past Progressive Tense: Describing an action that was interrupted by another event (The Past Progressive Tense) or completed in the past (The Simple Past Tense).
-
Use of ''Could'' (for Ability): Describing an ability in the past. -Use of ''Used to''): Describing past habits or routines that do not occur in the present. -Use of ''Would'' for past habits: Describing things which happen in the past as habit or repeated action but no longer happens.
-
Use of ''Wh- questions'' (How long, etc.): Asking for specific information about a subject, an object, time, a place, manner and a reason.
-
Use of Question Tags with Related Tenses: Asking short questions to confirm or clarify information in the sentence.
-
Use of Prepositions: (among, until, on, at, in, in case, by, of, with, about, to, for, from, out of): Indicating relationship among the components of a sentence in terms of cause, direction, manner, time, and location.
-
Use of Prepositional Phrases with in, for, from, to, at, about, with, from, of, etc.: Clarifying the details in the sentence about the cause, direction, manner, time, and location.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Healthy mind, healthy life!
Self-care isn’t selfish!
You’re stronger than you think!
I just need a break today!
Let’s chill for a bit!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
-
Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will explore the theme ''Personal Life and Well-Being'' by reflecting on how to maintain a balance between physical health, mental health, emotional health, and social health. Students will write a ''Well-Being Journal'' that includes daily entries for describing activities or habits that promote each aspect of well-being. The assignment will conclude with a reflection on how these components interconnect and suggestions for improving personal well-being in daily life. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To talk about personal well-being in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Well-being talk circles
Students work in groups and the teacher gives real-life well-being scenarios to discuss solutions by using the target grammar. For example, in the scenario, ''A person used to suffer from depression but stopped attending therapy'', students discuss questions such as: What was their situation like in the past? What could they have done to feel better? and How can they cope now? They provide responses such as: ''They used to attend therapy regularly'', ''They could try different strategies to cope with their anxiety'', and ''They were struggling with loneliness when they stopped therapy''. This activity encourages collaborative problemsolving and accurate use of grammar structures. In the end, the teacher gives feedback on the selection and use of language including target vocabulary and target grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To describe personal well-being in English by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Fill it in right
The teacher shows pictures of word groups such as ''suffer from, recover from, participate in, and talk to''. For example, a picture of someone ill with ''suffer from'' written on it or a person in a group with ''participate in''. Then, students receive a worksheet with sentences such as ''She suffered ___ loneliness'' or ''He participated ___ therapy''. They fill in the blanks, read their answers aloud, and the teacher gives feedback. In the end, students write one new sentence by using a preposition they learned. In the end, the teacher gives feedback on the selection and use of language including target vocabulary and target grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Physical health (body and illnesses); personal well-being with mental and emotional health; personal well-being with social health''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for personal well-being with physical health (body and illnesses):
Nouns: A lung, a joint, a heel, a consultant, healthcare, herb, hunger, a pill, recovery, a surgeon, survival, a first-aid kit, a bacterium, a cell, a mineral, relief, a surgery, a vitamin, a fever, a stroke, a cancer, a wound, an injury, anxiety, depression, an addiction, a recovery, a disability, panic, medication, an infection, a symptom, a treatment.
Verbs: To breathe, to consult, to heal, to cure, to suffer, to swallow, to operate, to bother.
Adjectives: Balanced, adequate, disabled, relieved, short-term, urgent, conscious, longterm, severe, unconscious.
Adverbs: Terribly, accidentally, adequately, appropriately, instantly, severely, strictly.
Vocabulary for personal well-being with mental and emotional health: Nouns: Mental health, psychological health, social bond/involvement, family tie, confidence, fulfilment, balance, self-awareness, empathy.
Vocabulary for practices and actions with mental and emotional health: Nouns: Mindfulness, therapy, breathing exercises, relaxation, rehabilitation.
Vocabulary for personal well-being with social health: Nouns: Loneliness, isolation, alienation, social anxiety, conflict, relief, pride, confusion, disappointment, trust, adaptation, acceptance.
Verbs: To interact, to socialise, to participate, to maintain, to contribute, to volunteer, to strengthen, to support.
Vocabulary for social relationship: Nouns: An acquaintance, a colleague, a community member, a mentor.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Past Tense versus the Past Progressive Tense: (She was suffering from a headache when her friend called her yesterday).
-
Could for Ability: (I could exercise for 30 minutes without interruption when I was younger).
-
Used to: (He used to socialise for his well-being).
-
Would: (When I was a kid, we would visit my grandparents every summer holiday).
-
Wh- questions (How long, etc.): (How long did your friend suffer from depression?).
-
Question Tags with Related Tenses: (She healed after the surgery, didn’t she?)
-
Prepositions: (among, until, on, at, in, in case, by, of, with, about, to, for, from, out of): (The consultant helped him cope with his depression).
-
Prepositional Phrases with in, for, to, at, about, with, from, of, etc.: (She struggled with frustration after the teacher announced the exam results).
-
Either, Neither, So do I, I hope so: (She can either take a short walk or do some breathing exercises to feel better). (Neither stress nor overthinking is good for your mental wellbeing). (I believe taking time for ourselves is important. So do I).(Doctors say regular exercise improves our health. I hope so!).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Past Tense versus the Past Progressive Tense: Describing an action that was interrupted by another event (The Past Progressive Tense) or completed in the past (The Simple Past Tense).
-
Use of ''Could'' (for Ability): Describing an ability in the past. -Use of ''Used to''): Describing past habits or routines that do not occur in the present. -Use of ''Would'' for past habits: Describing things which happen in the past as habit or repeated action but no longer happens.
-
Use of ''Wh- questions'' (How long, etc.): Asking for specific information about a subject, an object, time, a place, manner and a reason.
-
Use of Question Tags with Related Tenses: Asking short questions to confirm or clarify information in the sentence.
-
Use of Prepositions: (among, until, on, at, in, in case, by, of, with, about, to, for, from, out of): Indicating relationship among the components of a sentence in terms of cause, direction, manner, time, and location.
-
Use of Prepositional Phrases with in, for, from, to, at, about, with, from, of, etc.: Clarifying the details in the sentence about the cause, direction, manner, time, and location.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Healthy mind, healthy life!
Self-care isn’t selfish!
You’re stronger than you think!
I just need a break today!
Let’s chill for a bit!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
-
Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will explore the theme ''Personal Life and Well-Being'' by reflecting on how to maintain a balance between physical health, mental health, emotional health, and social health. Students will write a ''Well-Being Journal'' that includes daily entries for describing activities or habits that promote each aspect of well-being. The assignment will conclude with a reflection on how these components interconnect and suggestions for improving personal well-being in daily life. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To talk about personal well-being in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Well-being talk circles
Students work in groups and the teacher gives real-life well-being scenarios to discuss solutions by using the target grammar. For example, in the scenario, ''A person used to suffer from depression but stopped attending therapy'', students discuss questions such as: What was their situation like in the past? What could they have done to feel better? and How can they cope now? They provide responses such as: ''They used to attend therapy regularly'', ''They could try different strategies to cope with their anxiety'', and ''They were struggling with loneliness when they stopped therapy''. This activity encourages collaborative problemsolving and accurate use of grammar structures. In the end, the teacher gives feedback on the selection and use of language including target vocabulary and target grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To describe personal well-being in English by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Fill it in right
The teacher shows pictures of word groups such as ''suffer from, recover from, participate in, and talk to''. For example, a picture of someone ill with ''suffer from'' written on it or a person in a group with ''participate in''. Then, students receive a worksheet with sentences such as ''She suffered ___ loneliness'' or ''He participated ___ therapy''. They fill in the blanks, read their answers aloud, and the teacher gives feedback. In the end, students write one new sentence by using a preposition they learned. In the end, the teacher gives feedback on the selection and use of language including target vocabulary and target grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Past Tense versus the Past Progressive Tense: (She was suffering from a headache when her friend called her yesterday).
-
Could for Ability: (I could exercise for 30 minutes without interruption when I was younger).
-
Used to: (He used to socialise for his well-being).
-
Would: (When I was a kid, we would visit my grandparents every summer holiday).
-
Wh- questions (How long, etc.): (How long did your friend suffer from depression?).
-
Question Tags with Related Tenses: (She healed after the surgery, didn’t she?)
-
Prepositions: (among, until, on, at, in, in case, by, of, with, about, to, for, from, out of): (The consultant helped him cope with his depression).
-
Prepositional Phrases with in, for, to, at, about, with, from, of, etc.: (She struggled with frustration after the teacher announced the exam results).
-
Either, Neither, So do I, I hope so: (She can either take a short walk or do some breathing exercises to feel better). (Neither stress nor overthinking is good for your mental wellbeing). (I believe taking time for ourselves is important. So do I).(Doctors say regular exercise improves our health. I hope so!).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Past Tense versus the Past Progressive Tense: Describing an action that was interrupted by another event (The Past Progressive Tense) or completed in the past (The Simple Past Tense).
-
Use of ''Could'' (for Ability): Describing an ability in the past. -Use of ''Used to''): Describing past habits or routines that do not occur in the present. -Use of ''Would'' for past habits: Describing things which happen in the past as habit or repeated action but no longer happens.
-
Use of ''Wh- questions'' (How long, etc.): Asking for specific information about a subject, an object, time, a place, manner and a reason.
-
Use of Question Tags with Related Tenses: Asking short questions to confirm or clarify information in the sentence.
-
Use of Prepositions: (among, until, on, at, in, in case, by, of, with, about, to, for, from, out of): Indicating relationship among the components of a sentence in terms of cause, direction, manner, time, and location.
-
Use of Prepositional Phrases with in, for, from, to, at, about, with, from, of, etc.: Clarifying the details in the sentence about the cause, direction, manner, time, and location.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Healthy mind, healthy life!
Self-care isn’t selfish!
You’re stronger than you think!
I just need a break today!
Let’s chill for a bit!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
-
Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will explore the theme ''Personal Life and Well-Being'' by reflecting on how to maintain a balance between physical health, mental health, emotional health, and social health. Students will write a ''Well-Being Journal'' that includes daily entries for describing activities or habits that promote each aspect of well-being. The assignment will conclude with a reflection on how these components interconnect and suggestions for improving personal well-being in daily life. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
