EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To talk about global cuisines, food habits, and cultures in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1:
Students write a short paragraph about global cuisines or cultural diversity using at least five target vocabulary and grammatical items (e.g. modals for probability, necessity, or advice). For example, they might describe a dish such as Turkish Dolma (stuffed peppers) by explaining its ingredients, preparation, and cultural significance. After writing, they create a slide with visuals (e.g. a picture of the dish). Then they present their slide and paragraph to the class, explaining globalisation or cultural habits. The teacher provides feedback on the use of language including target vocabulary, grammar, and also their presentation skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about global cuisines and their impact on people in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Understanding Global Cuisines and Their Influence
The teacher prepares a short paragraph about global cuisines and their influence on people. Students read the paragraph and answer simple comprehension questions to practice target vocabulary and target grammar.
Reading Text (Simplified):
''Global cuisines are very popular today. People can try many different flavours such as spicy or sweet dishes from all over the world. For example, sushi is a famous Japanese dish made with rice and fish. To make it, chefs chop fresh ingredients and combine them carefully. Eating healthy food like sushi can be good for your nutrition. You should also avoid eating too much sugar because it may cause health problems like obesity. If you want to cook healthy meals, you need to use fresh and balanced ingredients''.
Questions:
1. True or False: Sushi is made with rice and fish.
2. What is a good example of healthy food from Japan?
3. Which word means ''too much weight'' because of unhealthy food?
4. Complete the sentence: ''To make sushi, chefs ______ fresh ingredients''.
Students read their answers aloud to the class. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on the use of language including accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Global cuisines, food habits and cultures; cultural diversity and international sports, films and musical events; impact of globalisation on everyday life''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary): Vocabulary for global cuisines, food habits and cultures: Nouns: Consumption, a combination, flavour, nutrition, obesity, a portion, a preference, protein, spice. Verbs: To chop, to manufacture, to swallow.
Adjectives: Affordable, balanced, beneficial, dairy, organic.
Vocabulary for cultural diversity and international sports events: Nouns: Conservation, a leaflet, a legend, a myth, a parade. Verbs: To adapt, to classify, to distinguish, to inherit.
Adjectives: Appropriate, mixed, precious. Adverbs: Genuinely. International sports events: Nouns: An applicant, a marathon, a medal, a membership, a referee, a spectator, a sponsorship, an opponent, a representative, a pitch, a venue.
Verbs: To broadcast, to cheer, to equip. Adjectives: Entertaining, risky, skilled. Adverbs: Severely.
Impact of globalisation on everyday life: Nouns: A civilization, fame. Verbs: To dominate, to edit, to exploit.
Adjectives: industrial, universal, widespread. Adverbs: Apparently, extensively, rapidly.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Modals for Probability: (''Can, Could, May, Might, Must''): (The combination of organic vegetables can provide a better source of nutrition).
-
Modals for Lack of Probability (''Can’t, Couldn’t''): (That can’t be dessert. It’s too sour!)
-
Modals for Speculation: (''Can, Could, May, Might, Must, Can’t, Couldn’t''): (She must be the assistant chef of this restaurant).
-
Modals for Deduction (''Must, Can’t, Might, May, Could''): (The meal must be high in protein because it’s made of meat).
-
Modals for Obligation and Necessity (''Must, Have to, Need'') Obligation in the Past (''Had to''): (They must wash their hands before cooking the food).
-
Modals for lack of Obligation (''Don’t have to- Don’t need to, Needn’t''): (You don’t have to eat that soup if it doesn’t taste good).
-
Modals for Prohibition (''Must not - Can’t''): (You can’t enter the kitchen. You don’t work here). -Modals for Lack of Prohibition (Modals for Permission) (''Can, may, could''): (You could learn the recipe if you like).
-
Modals for Advice (''Should, Ought to, Had better, Could''): (You should try Turkish ''Dolma'' if you want to taste traditional food in Türkiye)
-
Be Able to in the Present and Future: (People will be able to reach global markets more easily due to developments in technology in the future).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of Modals (''Can, Could, May, Might, Must''): Expressing probability and speculation.
-
Use of Modals (''Can’t, Couldn’t''): Expressing lack of Probability. -Use of Modals (''Could, Must, Can’t, Might, May''): Expressing deduction.
-
Use of Modals (''Must, Have to, Need'') Obligation in the Past (''Had to''): Expressing obligation and necessity.
-
Use of Modals (''Don’t have to, Don’t need to, Needn’t''): Expressing lack of obligation.
-
Use of Modals (''Must not - Can’t''): Expressing prohibition. -Use of Modals (Modals for Permission) (''Can, may, could''): Expressing lack of prohibition.
-
Modals for Advice (''Should, Ought to, Had better, Could''): Expressing advice and recommendation.
-
Use of ''Be Able to in the Present and Future'' (''Am-is-are able to, will be able to'': Expressing ability.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
That’s part of our tradition!
Let me show you something from our culture!
Different is interesting, not weird!
Culture brings us closer!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: o
Consonants: l, m, n, (ng), p
Vowel: o: (/əʊ/, /ɒ/, /əʊ/)
Consonants: l: (/ɛl/ /l/, silent /l/); m; (/ɛm/,/m/); n: (/ɛn/, /n/, silent /n/); ng: (/ng/); p: (piː//p/, silent /p/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will explore the theme ''Life in the World and Culture'' by focusing on global cuisines, food habits, and cultures, cultural diversity through international sports, films, and musical events, and the impact of globalisation on everyday life. Students will design ''a cultural portfolio'' in which they choose one country to research and present its unique food traditions, popular cultural events, and important contributions to global sports or arts. They will also examine how globalisation has influenced these traditions, such as the fusion of cuisines or the international popularity of certain sports and films. The portfolio will include visuals, descriptions, and personal reflections on what they have learnt about the interconnectedness of cultures worldwide. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To talk about global cuisines, food habits, and cultures in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1:
Students write a short paragraph about global cuisines or cultural diversity using at least five target vocabulary and grammatical items (e.g. modals for probability, necessity, or advice). For example, they might describe a dish such as Turkish Dolma (stuffed peppers) by explaining its ingredients, preparation, and cultural significance. After writing, they create a slide with visuals (e.g. a picture of the dish). Then they present their slide and paragraph to the class, explaining globalisation or cultural habits. The teacher provides feedback on the use of language including target vocabulary, grammar, and also their presentation skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about global cuisines and their impact on people in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Understanding Global Cuisines and Their Influence
The teacher prepares a short paragraph about global cuisines and their influence on people. Students read the paragraph and answer simple comprehension questions to practice target vocabulary and target grammar.
Reading Text (Simplified):
''Global cuisines are very popular today. People can try many different flavours such as spicy or sweet dishes from all over the world. For example, sushi is a famous Japanese dish made with rice and fish. To make it, chefs chop fresh ingredients and combine them carefully. Eating healthy food like sushi can be good for your nutrition. You should also avoid eating too much sugar because it may cause health problems like obesity. If you want to cook healthy meals, you need to use fresh and balanced ingredients''.
Questions:
1. True or False: Sushi is made with rice and fish.
2. What is a good example of healthy food from Japan?
3. Which word means ''too much weight'' because of unhealthy food?
4. Complete the sentence: ''To make sushi, chefs ______ fresh ingredients''.
Students read their answers aloud to the class. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on the use of language including accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Modals for Probability: (''Can, Could, May, Might, Must''): (The combination of organic vegetables can provide a better source of nutrition).
-
Modals for Lack of Probability (''Can’t, Couldn’t''): (That can’t be dessert. It’s too sour!)
-
Modals for Speculation: (''Can, Could, May, Might, Must, Can’t, Couldn’t''): (She must be the assistant chef of this restaurant).
-
Modals for Deduction (''Must, Can’t, Might, May, Could''): (The meal must be high in protein because it’s made of meat).
-
Modals for Obligation and Necessity (''Must, Have to, Need'') Obligation in the Past (''Had to''): (They must wash their hands before cooking the food).
-
Modals for lack of Obligation (''Don’t have to- Don’t need to, Needn’t''): (You don’t have to eat that soup if it doesn’t taste good).
-
Modals for Prohibition (''Must not - Can’t''): (You can’t enter the kitchen. You don’t work here). -Modals for Lack of Prohibition (Modals for Permission) (''Can, may, could''): (You could learn the recipe if you like).
-
Modals for Advice (''Should, Ought to, Had better, Could''): (You should try Turkish ''Dolma'' if you want to taste traditional food in Türkiye)
-
Be Able to in the Present and Future: (People will be able to reach global markets more easily due to developments in technology in the future).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of Modals (''Can, Could, May, Might, Must''): Expressing probability and speculation.
-
Use of Modals (''Can’t, Couldn’t''): Expressing lack of Probability. -Use of Modals (''Could, Must, Can’t, Might, May''): Expressing deduction.
-
Use of Modals (''Must, Have to, Need'') Obligation in the Past (''Had to''): Expressing obligation and necessity.
-
Use of Modals (''Don’t have to, Don’t need to, Needn’t''): Expressing lack of obligation.
-
Use of Modals (''Must not - Can’t''): Expressing prohibition. -Use of Modals (Modals for Permission) (''Can, may, could''): Expressing lack of prohibition.
-
Modals for Advice (''Should, Ought to, Had better, Could''): Expressing advice and recommendation.
-
Use of ''Be Able to in the Present and Future'' (''Am-is-are able to, will be able to'': Expressing ability.

Culture brings us closer!

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will explore the theme ''Life in the World and Culture'' by focusing on global cuisines, food habits, and cultures, cultural diversity through international sports, films, and musical events, and the impact of globalisation on everyday life. Students will design ''a cultural portfolio'' in which they choose one country to research and present its unique food traditions, popular cultural events, and important contributions to global sports or arts. They will also examine how globalisation has influenced these traditions, such as the fusion of cuisines or the international popularity of certain sports and films. The portfolio will include visuals, descriptions, and personal reflections on what they have learnt about the interconnectedness of cultures worldwide. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will search for the theme ''Life in Nature and Global Problems'' by examining the effects of humans on natural disasters and effects of natural disasters on nature and humans and the role of technology in addressing global issues such as healthcare, AI, and data solutions. Students will research a specific natural disaster for the details of its environmental and human impact and suggest innovative solutions for being prepared for disasters or recovery by using modern technology. They will design a multimedia presentation or poster showing how technological developments such as AI for disaster prediction can lessen the effects of these disasters. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To talk about global cuisines, food habits, and cultures in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1:
Students write a short paragraph about global cuisines or cultural diversity using at least five target vocabulary and grammatical items (e.g. modals for probability, necessity, or advice). For example, they might describe a dish such as Turkish Dolma (stuffed peppers) by explaining its ingredients, preparation, and cultural significance. After writing, they create a slide with visuals (e.g. a picture of the dish). Then they present their slide and paragraph to the class, explaining globalisation or cultural habits. The teacher provides feedback on the use of language including target vocabulary, grammar, and also their presentation skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about global cuisines and their impact on people in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Understanding Global Cuisines and Their Influence
The teacher prepares a short paragraph about global cuisines and their influence on people. Students read the paragraph and answer simple comprehension questions to practice target vocabulary and target grammar.
Reading Text (Simplified):
''Global cuisines are very popular today. People can try many different flavours such as spicy or sweet dishes from all over the world. For example, sushi is a famous Japanese dish made with rice and fish. To make it, chefs chop fresh ingredients and combine them carefully. Eating healthy food like sushi can be good for your nutrition. You should also avoid eating too much sugar because it may cause health problems like obesity. If you want to cook healthy meals, you need to use fresh and balanced ingredients''.
Questions:
1. True or False: Sushi is made with rice and fish.
2. What is a good example of healthy food from Japan?
3. Which word means ''too much weight'' because of unhealthy food?
4. Complete the sentence: ''To make sushi, chefs ______ fresh ingredients''.
Students read their answers aloud to the class. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on the use of language including accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Objective: To talk about natural disasters and their influence on nature; natural disasters and their influence on humans in English by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Disaster Response Simulation
Students work in small groups, and the teacher assigns each group a disaster scenario (e.g. a flood destroying a village, a volcanic eruption threatening a town). Within each group, students take roles such as ''Emergency Responder, Local Authority, Environmental Scientist, and Survivor''. They role-play a meeting to discuss the disaster’s effects by using target vocabulary (e.g. rescue, destruction, survival) and target grammar (e.g. ''The flood, which destroyed our homes, left us desperate for help''). After their discussions, groups present a summary to the class, and the teacher gives feedback on use of vocabulary, grammar, and also of communication. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Objective: To talk about natural disasters and their impact on nature in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Match and design
Students work in small groups, and the teacher provides each group with two sets of cards: one with target vocabulary (e.g. earthquake, habitat, harm) and another with their definitions. Groups match the words with the correct definitions. After matching, each group selects 3-4 words and makes sentences by using them, encouraging the use of relative clauses (which, who, that) when possible. For example: ''The earthquake that struck the city caused great damage''. Groups share their sentences with the class, and the teacher gives feedback on the use of grammar and vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.ÜNİTE:
THEME 7: LIFE IN NATURE & GLOBAL
PROBLEMS
plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Natural disasters and their impact on nature; natural disasters and their impact on humans; impact of technology on global issues (AI, data, healthcare)''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for natural disasters and their impact on nature
Natural disasters: An earthquake, a volcanic eruption, a tsunami, a landslide, an avalanche, a flood, erosion, a hurricane, a tornado.
Natural disasters’ impact on nature: Nouns: A habitat, a cliff, wildlife, species. Verbs: To harm, to erupt, to ruin. Adjectives: Widespread, inevitable. Adverbs: Inevitably.
Vocabulary for natural disasters and their impact on humans: Nouns: An aid, a disorder, duration, a firefighter, hunger, a kit, panic, pity, shortage, a survival, a survivor, a tragedy.
Verbs: To anticipate, to cope, to forecast, to overcome, to rescue, to strengthen.
Adjectives: Anxious, desperate, homeless, miserable, tragic, severe, unfortunate, urgent.
Adverbs: Desperately, dramatically.
Vocabulary for impact of technology on global issues: Nouns: Healthcare, trading, a device, a recovery. Verbs: To heal, to cure, to maintain, to obtain, to progress. Adjectives: Wise. Adverbs: Primarily, efficiently, likewise.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Relative Pronouns Used for Relative Clauses: (Which, Who, That) (Defining and Non-defining): (The earthquake that damaged the village caused many inhabitants to become homeless. The survivor, who lost their entire family in the flood, showed great resilience).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Relative Pronouns Used for Relative Clauses: (Which, Who, That) (Defining and Non-defining):
-
Use of Defining Relative Clauses: (Which, Who, That): Referring to objects or things by providing essential information that identifies them.
-
Use of Non-defining Relative Clauses: (Which, Who, That): Referring to objects or things by adding extra, non-essential information without changing the core meaning of the sentence.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Let’s not waste anything on this planet! We should do something for the Earth, even if it’s small. That earthquake was scary! Small actions matter for our world! We have to protect what we’ve got on this planet!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: u
Consonants: q, r, s, t
Vowel: u: (/juː/, /ʌ/, /juː/, silent /u/)
Consonants: q: (/kjuː/, /k/); r: (/ɑː/(Br), silent /r/ (Br), /aɹ/ (AmE), /ɹ/ (AmE), silent /r/ (Br)); s: (/s/, /ɛs/, /z/, silent /s/); t : (/tiː/, /t/, silent /t/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will search for the theme ''Life in Nature and Global Problems'' by examining the effects of humans on natural disasters and effects of natural disasters on nature and humans and the role of technology in addressing global issues such as healthcare, AI, and data solutions. Students will research a specific natural disaster for the details of its environmental and human impact and suggest innovative solutions for being prepared for disasters or recovery by using modern technology. They will design a multimedia presentation or poster showing how technological developments such as AI for disaster prediction can lessen the effects of these disasters. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To talk about natural disasters and their influence on nature; natural disasters and their influence on humans in English by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Disaster Response Simulation
Students work in small groups, and the teacher assigns each group a disaster scenario (e.g. a flood destroying a village, a volcanic eruption threatening a town). Within each group, students take roles such as ''Emergency Responder, Local Authority, Environmental Scientist, and Survivor''. They role-play a meeting to discuss the disaster’s effects by using target vocabulary (e.g. rescue, destruction, survival) and target grammar (e.g. ''The flood, which destroyed our homes, left us desperate for help''). After their discussions, groups present a summary to the class, and the teacher gives feedback on use of vocabulary, grammar, and also of communication. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about natural disasters and their impact on nature in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Match and design
Students work in small groups, and the teacher provides each group with two sets of cards: one with target vocabulary (e.g. earthquake, habitat, harm) and another with their definitions. Groups match the words with the correct definitions. After matching, each group selects 3-4 words and makes sentences by using them, encouraging the use of relative clauses (which, who, that) when possible. For example: ''The earthquake that struck the city caused great damage''. Groups share their sentences with the class, and the teacher gives feedback on the use of grammar and vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.ÜNİTE:
THEME 7: LIFE IN NATURE & GLOBAL
PROBLEMS
plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Natural disasters and their impact on nature; natural disasters and their impact on humans; impact of technology on global issues (AI, data, healthcare)''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for natural disasters and their impact on nature
Natural disasters: An earthquake, a volcanic eruption, a tsunami, a landslide, an avalanche, a flood, erosion, a hurricane, a tornado.
Natural disasters’ impact on nature: Nouns: A habitat, a cliff, wildlife, species. Verbs: To harm, to erupt, to ruin. Adjectives: Widespread, inevitable. Adverbs: Inevitably.
Vocabulary for natural disasters and their impact on humans: Nouns: An aid, a disorder, duration, a firefighter, hunger, a kit, panic, pity, shortage, a survival, a survivor, a tragedy.
Verbs: To anticipate, to cope, to forecast, to overcome, to rescue, to strengthen.
Adjectives: Anxious, desperate, homeless, miserable, tragic, severe, unfortunate, urgent.
Adverbs: Desperately, dramatically.
Vocabulary for impact of technology on global issues: Nouns: Healthcare, trading, a device, a recovery. Verbs: To heal, to cure, to maintain, to obtain, to progress. Adjectives: Wise. Adverbs: Primarily, efficiently, likewise.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Relative Pronouns Used for Relative Clauses: (Which, Who, That) (Defining and Non-defining): (The earthquake that damaged the village caused many inhabitants to become homeless. The survivor, who lost their entire family in the flood, showed great resilience).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Relative Pronouns Used for Relative Clauses: (Which, Who, That) (Defining and Non-defining):
-
Use of Defining Relative Clauses: (Which, Who, That): Referring to objects or things by providing essential information that identifies them.
-
Use of Non-defining Relative Clauses: (Which, Who, That): Referring to objects or things by adding extra, non-essential information without changing the core meaning of the sentence.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Let’s not waste anything on this planet! We should do something for the Earth, even if it’s small. That earthquake was scary! Small actions matter for our world! We have to protect what we’ve got on this planet!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: u
Consonants: q, r, s, t
Vowel: u: (/juː/, /ʌ/, /juː/, silent /u/)
Consonants: q: (/kjuː/, /k/); r: (/ɑː/(Br), silent /r/ (Br), /aɹ/ (AmE), /ɹ/ (AmE), silent /r/ (Br)); s: (/s/, /ɛs/, /z/, silent /s/); t : (/tiː/, /t/, silent /t/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will search for the theme ''Life in Nature and Global Problems'' by examining the effects of humans on natural disasters and effects of natural disasters on nature and humans and the role of technology in addressing global issues such as healthcare, AI, and data solutions. Students will research a specific natural disaster for the details of its environmental and human impact and suggest innovative solutions for being prepared for disasters or recovery by using modern technology. They will design a multimedia presentation or poster showing how technological developments such as AI for disaster prediction can lessen the effects of these disasters. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To talk about natural disasters and their influence on nature; natural disasters and their influence on humans in English by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Disaster Response Simulation
Students work in small groups, and the teacher assigns each group a disaster scenario (e.g. a flood destroying a village, a volcanic eruption threatening a town). Within each group, students take roles such as ''Emergency Responder, Local Authority, Environmental Scientist, and Survivor''. They role-play a meeting to discuss the disaster’s effects by using target vocabulary (e.g. rescue, destruction, survival) and target grammar (e.g. ''The flood, which destroyed our homes, left us desperate for help''). After their discussions, groups present a summary to the class, and the teacher gives feedback on use of vocabulary, grammar, and also of communication. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about natural disasters and their impact on nature in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Match and design
Students work in small groups, and the teacher provides each group with two sets of cards: one with target vocabulary (e.g. earthquake, habitat, harm) and another with their definitions. Groups match the words with the correct definitions. After matching, each group selects 3-4 words and makes sentences by using them, encouraging the use of relative clauses (which, who, that) when possible. For example: ''The earthquake that struck the city caused great damage''. Groups share their sentences with the class, and the teacher gives feedback on the use of grammar and vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.ÜNİTE:
THEME 7: LIFE IN NATURE & GLOBAL
PROBLEMS
plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Natural disasters and their impact on nature; natural disasters and their impact on humans; impact of technology on global issues (AI, data, healthcare)''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for natural disasters and their impact on nature
Natural disasters: An earthquake, a volcanic eruption, a tsunami, a landslide, an avalanche, a flood, erosion, a hurricane, a tornado.
Natural disasters’ impact on nature: Nouns: A habitat, a cliff, wildlife, species. Verbs: To harm, to erupt, to ruin. Adjectives: Widespread, inevitable. Adverbs: Inevitably.
Vocabulary for natural disasters and their impact on humans: Nouns: An aid, a disorder, duration, a firefighter, hunger, a kit, panic, pity, shortage, a survival, a survivor, a tragedy.
Verbs: To anticipate, to cope, to forecast, to overcome, to rescue, to strengthen.
Adjectives: Anxious, desperate, homeless, miserable, tragic, severe, unfortunate, urgent.
Adverbs: Desperately, dramatically.
Vocabulary for impact of technology on global issues: Nouns: Healthcare, trading, a device, a recovery. Verbs: To heal, to cure, to maintain, to obtain, to progress. Adjectives: Wise. Adverbs: Primarily, efficiently, likewise.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Relative Pronouns Used for Relative Clauses: (Which, Who, That) (Defining and Non-defining): (The earthquake that damaged the village caused many inhabitants to become homeless. The survivor, who lost their entire family in the flood, showed great resilience).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Relative Pronouns Used for Relative Clauses: (Which, Who, That) (Defining and Non-defining):
-
Use of Defining Relative Clauses: (Which, Who, That): Referring to objects or things by providing essential information that identifies them.
-
Use of Non-defining Relative Clauses: (Which, Who, That): Referring to objects or things by adding extra, non-essential information without changing the core meaning of the sentence.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Let’s not waste anything on this planet! We should do something for the Earth, even if it’s small. That earthquake was scary! Small actions matter for our world! We have to protect what we’ve got on this planet!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: u
Consonants: q, r, s, t
Vowel: u: (/juː/, /ʌ/, /juː/, silent /u/)
Consonants: q: (/kjuː/, /k/); r: (/ɑː/(Br), silent /r/ (Br), /aɹ/ (AmE), /ɹ/ (AmE), silent /r/ (Br)); s: (/s/, /ɛs/, /z/, silent /s/); t : (/tiː/, /t/, silent /t/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will search for the theme ''Life in Nature and Global Problems'' by examining the effects of humans on natural disasters and effects of natural disasters on nature and humans and the role of technology in addressing global issues such as healthcare, AI, and data solutions. Students will research a specific natural disaster for the details of its environmental and human impact and suggest innovative solutions for being prepared for disasters or recovery by using modern technology. They will design a multimedia presentation or poster showing how technological developments such as AI for disaster prediction can lessen the effects of these disasters. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To talk about natural disasters and their influence on nature; natural disasters and their influence on humans in English by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Disaster Response Simulation
Students work in small groups, and the teacher assigns each group a disaster scenario (e.g. a flood destroying a village, a volcanic eruption threatening a town). Within each group, students take roles such as ''Emergency Responder, Local Authority, Environmental Scientist, and Survivor''. They role-play a meeting to discuss the disaster’s effects by using target vocabulary (e.g. rescue, destruction, survival) and target grammar (e.g. ''The flood, which destroyed our homes, left us desperate for help''). After their discussions, groups present a summary to the class, and the teacher gives feedback on use of vocabulary, grammar, and also of communication. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about natural disasters and their impact on nature in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Match and design
Students work in small groups, and the teacher provides each group with two sets of cards: one with target vocabulary (e.g. earthquake, habitat, harm) and another with their definitions. Groups match the words with the correct definitions. After matching, each group selects 3-4 words and makes sentences by using them, encouraging the use of relative clauses (which, who, that) when possible. For example: ''The earthquake that struck the city caused great damage''. Groups share their sentences with the class, and the teacher gives feedback on the use of grammar and vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.ÜNİTE:
THEME 8: LIFE IN THE UNIVERSE & THE
FUTURE
plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Universal issues in the future; search for habitable planets; space and technology''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for life in the universe: Nouns: Globe, oxygen, carbon, observation. Verbs: To observe. Adjectives: Mysterious, solar, essential, external, outer, unknown. Adverbs: Essentially, universally.
Vocabulary for habitable planets: Nouns: Existence, an exploration, an inhabitant, an astronomer, a civilisation, a mission, a satellite, a rocket, a colony, radiation. Verbs: To attempt, to estimate, to detect, to launch, to settle. Adjectives: Distant, dynamic, massive, potential. Adverbs: Beyond, potentially, elsewhere. Vocabulary for space and technology: Nouns: An alien, a database, an aircraft, privacy, navigation. Verbs: To implement, to interact, to install, to advance, to transform.
Adjectives: Sophisticated, efficient, curious, artificial.
Phrases: Space mission, interplanetary travel
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Zero Conditional: (If you heat water to 100 degrees Celsius, it boils).
-
Conditional 1: (If we leave early in the morning, we will have enough time to explore the city centre).
-
Conditional 2: (If we found another planet to live on, would people travel there?).
-
Wish Clauses: (I wish our planet could be a better place to live).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Zero Conditional: Describing general truths, facts, and habits-situations where the result always happens if the condition is met.
-
Use of the Conditional 1: Describing realistic situations in future that are likely to happen and/or cause-andeffect relationship between a condition and its probable outcome.
-
Use of the Conditional 2: Describing imaginary, unlikely, and unreal situations in the present or future and their results.
-
Use of ''Wish Clauses'': Describing regrets, desires, and/or unreal situations about the present, future and the past.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
What do you think the future will be like?
Would you go to space if you could?
Sounds like sci-fi - but maybe not.
The future is closer than we think!
Big ideas start with small questions!

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will work on and examine the theme ''Life in the Universe and the Future'' by searching universal issues in the future, the search for habitable planets, and advancements in space and technology. They will imagine what life could look like in the next century by focusing on how humanity could address challenges such as overpopulation, resource consumption, and environmental crises. Students will research current efforts to discover habitable planets and create a futuristic journal entry. They can enlarge their entry by a model of an advanced technology that could solve a universal issue or expand space exploration. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/ or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To describe habitable planets, space exploration, and technology about planets and space in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing
The teacher provides students with an incomplete paragraph about habitable planets and developments in space technology. For example: ''The search for habitable planets has become the main focus for astronomers and space agencies worldwide. With the launch of advanced satellites and exploration missions, scientists are able to detect potential habitats now beyond our solar system. The development of artificial intelligence and sophisticated navigation systems has made these missions more efficient. However, the challenge is still present such as the resources are limited and environmental conditions are difficult. If humans achieve self-sustaining colonies, __________''.
Students work individually or in pairs to complete the paragraph by emphasising creativity and using target vocabulary such as ''civilisation, exploration, radiation, vast, dynamic, potentially''. After completing their work they present their paragraphs to the class. The teacher checks and gives feedback on the use of language with target vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about possible future scenarios in space exploration in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing
The teacher shows some flashcards with visuals representing target vocabulary such as ''rocket, colony, AI, radiation, habitat'' and asks students to match the visuals with the correct words written on the board. When the matching activity is complete students work to complete a worksheet with target grammar in pairs. They use the matched vocabulary to fill in the blanks in sentences such as ''If humans colonise distant planets, civilisations will emerge there'' or ''If we explore the universe, we might discover unknown habitats''. The teacher checks and gives feedback on the use of language including target vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

THEME 8: LIFE IN THE UNIVERSE & THE
FUTURE

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Universal issues in the future; search for habitable planets; space and technology''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for life in the universe: Nouns: Globe, oxygen, carbon, observation. Verbs: To observe. Adjectives: Mysterious, solar, essential, external, outer, unknown. Adverbs: Essentially, universally.
Vocabulary for habitable planets: Nouns: Existence, an exploration, an inhabitant, an astronomer, a civilisation, a mission, a satellite, a rocket, a colony, radiation. Verbs: To attempt, to estimate, to detect, to launch, to settle. Adjectives: Distant, dynamic, massive, potential. Adverbs: Beyond, potentially, elsewhere. Vocabulary for space and technology: Nouns: An alien, a database, an aircraft, privacy, navigation. Verbs: To implement, to interact, to install, to advance, to transform.
Adjectives: Sophisticated, efficient, curious, artificial.
Phrases: Space mission, interplanetary travel
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Zero Conditional: (If you heat water to 100 degrees Celsius, it boils).
-
Conditional 1: (If we leave early in the morning, we will have enough time to explore the city centre).
-
Conditional 2: (If we found another planet to live on, would people travel there?).
-
Wish Clauses: (I wish our planet could be a better place to live).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Zero Conditional: Describing general truths, facts, and habits-situations where the result always happens if the condition is met.
-
Use of the Conditional 1: Describing realistic situations in future that are likely to happen and/or cause-andeffect relationship between a condition and its probable outcome.
-
Use of the Conditional 2: Describing imaginary, unlikely, and unreal situations in the present or future and their results.
-
Use of ''Wish Clauses'': Describing regrets, desires, and/or unreal situations about the present, future and the past.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
What do you think the future will be like?
Would you go to space if you could?
Sounds like sci-fi - but maybe not.
The future is closer than we think!
Big ideas start with small questions!

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will work on and examine the theme ''Life in the Universe and the Future'' by searching universal issues in the future, the search for habitable planets, and advancements in space and technology. They will imagine what life could look like in the next century by focusing on how humanity could address challenges such as overpopulation, resource consumption, and environmental crises. Students will research current efforts to discover habitable planets and create a futuristic journal entry. They can enlarge their entry by a model of an advanced technology that could solve a universal issue or expand space exploration. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/ or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To describe habitable planets, space exploration, and technology about planets and space in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing
The teacher provides students with an incomplete paragraph about habitable planets and developments in space technology. For example: ''The search for habitable planets has become the main focus for astronomers and space agencies worldwide. With the launch of advanced satellites and exploration missions, scientists are able to detect potential habitats now beyond our solar system. The development of artificial intelligence and sophisticated navigation systems has made these missions more efficient. However, the challenge is still present such as the resources are limited and environmental conditions are difficult. If humans achieve self-sustaining colonies, __________''.
Students work individually or in pairs to complete the paragraph by emphasising creativity and using target vocabulary such as ''civilisation, exploration, radiation, vast, dynamic, potentially''. After completing their work they present their paragraphs to the class. The teacher checks and gives feedback on the use of language with target vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about possible future scenarios in space exploration in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing
The teacher shows some flashcards with visuals representing target vocabulary such as ''rocket, colony, AI, radiation, habitat'' and asks students to match the visuals with the correct words written on the board. When the matching activity is complete students work to complete a worksheet with target grammar in pairs. They use the matched vocabulary to fill in the blanks in sentences such as ''If humans colonise distant planets, civilisations will emerge there'' or ''If we explore the universe, we might discover unknown habitats''. The teacher checks and gives feedback on the use of language including target vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Universal issues in the future; search for habitable planets; space and technology''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for life in the universe: Nouns: Globe, oxygen, carbon, observation. Verbs: To observe. Adjectives: Mysterious, solar, essential, external, outer, unknown. Adverbs: Essentially, universally.
Vocabulary for habitable planets: Nouns: Existence, an exploration, an inhabitant, an astronomer, a civilisation, a mission, a satellite, a rocket, a colony, radiation. Verbs: To attempt, to estimate, to detect, to launch, to settle. Adjectives: Distant, dynamic, massive, potential. Adverbs: Beyond, potentially, elsewhere. Vocabulary for space and technology: Nouns: An alien, a database, an aircraft, privacy, navigation. Verbs: To implement, to interact, to install, to advance, to transform.
Adjectives: Sophisticated, efficient, curious, artificial.
Phrases: Space mission, interplanetary travel
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Zero Conditional: (If you heat water to 100 degrees Celsius, it boils).
-
Conditional 1: (If we leave early in the morning, we will have enough time to explore the city centre).
-
Conditional 2: (If we found another planet to live on, would people travel there?).
-
Wish Clauses: (I wish our planet could be a better place to live).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Zero Conditional: Describing general truths, facts, and habits-situations where the result always happens if the condition is met.
-
Use of the Conditional 1: Describing realistic situations in future that are likely to happen and/or cause-andeffect relationship between a condition and its probable outcome.
-
Use of the Conditional 2: Describing imaginary, unlikely, and unreal situations in the present or future and their results.
-
Use of ''Wish Clauses'': Describing regrets, desires, and/or unreal situations about the present, future and the past.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
What do you think the future will be like?
Would you go to space if you could?
Sounds like sci-fi - but maybe not.
The future is closer than we think!
Big ideas start with small questions!

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will work on and examine the theme ''Life in the Universe and the Future'' by searching universal issues in the future, the search for habitable planets, and advancements in space and technology. They will imagine what life could look like in the next century by focusing on how humanity could address challenges such as overpopulation, resource consumption, and environmental crises. Students will research current efforts to discover habitable planets and create a futuristic journal entry. They can enlarge their entry by a model of an advanced technology that could solve a universal issue or expand space exploration. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/ or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To describe habitable planets, space exploration, and technology about planets and space in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing
The teacher provides students with an incomplete paragraph about habitable planets and developments in space technology. For example: ''The search for habitable planets has become the main focus for astronomers and space agencies worldwide. With the launch of advanced satellites and exploration missions, scientists are able to detect potential habitats now beyond our solar system. The development of artificial intelligence and sophisticated navigation systems has made these missions more efficient. However, the challenge is still present such as the resources are limited and environmental conditions are difficult. If humans achieve self-sustaining colonies, __________''.
Students work individually or in pairs to complete the paragraph by emphasising creativity and using target vocabulary such as ''civilisation, exploration, radiation, vast, dynamic, potentially''. After completing their work they present their paragraphs to the class. The teacher checks and gives feedback on the use of language with target vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about possible future scenarios in space exploration in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing
The teacher shows some flashcards with visuals representing target vocabulary such as ''rocket, colony, AI, radiation, habitat'' and asks students to match the visuals with the correct words written on the board. When the matching activity is complete students work to complete a worksheet with target grammar in pairs. They use the matched vocabulary to fill in the blanks in sentences such as ''If humans colonise distant planets, civilisations will emerge there'' or ''If we explore the universe, we might discover unknown habitats''. The teacher checks and gives feedback on the use of language including target vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.ÜNİTE:
THEME 8: LIFE IN THE UNIVERSE & THE
FUTURE
plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Universal issues in the future; search for habitable planets; space and technology''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for life in the universe: Nouns: Globe, oxygen, carbon, observation. Verbs: To observe. Adjectives: Mysterious, solar, essential, external, outer, unknown. Adverbs: Essentially, universally.
Vocabulary for habitable planets: Nouns: Existence, an exploration, an inhabitant, an astronomer, a civilisation, a mission, a satellite, a rocket, a colony, radiation. Verbs: To attempt, to estimate, to detect, to launch, to settle. Adjectives: Distant, dynamic, massive, potential. Adverbs: Beyond, potentially, elsewhere. Vocabulary for space and technology: Nouns: An alien, a database, an aircraft, privacy, navigation. Verbs: To implement, to interact, to install, to advance, to transform.
Adjectives: Sophisticated, efficient, curious, artificial.
Phrases: Space mission, interplanetary travel
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Zero Conditional: (If you heat water to 100 degrees Celsius, it boils).
-
Conditional 1: (If we leave early in the morning, we will have enough time to explore the city centre).
-
Conditional 2: (If we found another planet to live on, would people travel there?).
-
Wish Clauses: (I wish our planet could be a better place to live).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Zero Conditional: Describing general truths, facts, and habits-situations where the result always happens if the condition is met.
-
Use of the Conditional 1: Describing realistic situations in future that are likely to happen and/or cause-andeffect relationship between a condition and its probable outcome.
-
Use of the Conditional 2: Describing imaginary, unlikely, and unreal situations in the present or future and their results.
-
Use of ''Wish Clauses'': Describing regrets, desires, and/or unreal situations about the present, future and the past.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
What do you think the future will be like?
Would you go to space if you could?
Sounds like sci-fi - but maybe not.
The future is closer than we think!
Big ideas start with small questions!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Consonants: v, w, x, y, z
Consonants: v: (/viː/, /v/); w: (/w/), silent /w/); x: (/ɛks/, /ks/, /gz/); y: (/waɪ/, /j/, /ɪ/, /iː/); z: /(zed/ (Br), /ziː/ (AmE), /z/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will work on and examine the theme ''Life in the Universe and the Future'' by searching universal issues in the future, the search for habitable planets, and advancements in space and technology. They will imagine what life could look like in the next century by focusing on how humanity could address challenges such as overpopulation, resource consumption, and environmental crises. Students will research current efforts to discover habitable planets and create a futuristic journal entry. They can enlarge their entry by a model of an advanced technology that could solve a universal issue or expand space exploration. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/ or a marking scheme.

EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
EXPANSION
Objective: To describe habitable planets, space exploration, and technology about planets and space in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing
The teacher provides students with an incomplete paragraph about habitable planets and developments in space technology. For example: ''The search for habitable planets has become the main focus for astronomers and space agencies worldwide. With the launch of advanced satellites and exploration missions, scientists are able to detect potential habitats now beyond our solar system. The development of artificial intelligence and sophisticated navigation systems has made these missions more efficient. However, the challenge is still present such as the resources are limited and environmental conditions are difficult. If humans achieve self-sustaining colonies, __________''.
Students work individually or in pairs to complete the paragraph by emphasising creativity and using target vocabulary such as ''civilisation, exploration, radiation, vast, dynamic, potentially''. After completing their work they present their paragraphs to the class. The teacher checks and gives feedback on the use of language with target vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about possible future scenarios in space exploration in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing
The teacher shows some flashcards with visuals representing target vocabulary such as ''rocket, colony, AI, radiation, habitat'' and asks students to match the visuals with the correct words written on the board. When the matching activity is complete students work to complete a worksheet with target grammar in pairs. They use the matched vocabulary to fill in the blanks in sentences such as ''If humans colonise distant planets, civilisations will emerge there'' or ''If we explore the universe, we might discover unknown habitats''. The teacher checks and gives feedback on the use of language including target vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will work on and examine the theme ''Life in the Universe and the Future'' by searching universal issues in the future, the search for habitable planets, and advancements in space and technology. They will imagine what life could look like in the next century by focusing on how humanity could address challenges such as overpopulation, resource consumption, and environmental crises. Students will research current efforts to discover habitable planets and create a futuristic journal entry. They can enlarge their entry by a model of an advanced technology that could solve a universal issue or expand space exploration. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/ or a marking scheme.

EXPANSION
Objective: To describe habitable planets, space exploration, and technology about planets and space in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing
The teacher provides students with an incomplete paragraph about habitable planets and developments in space technology. For example: ''The search for habitable planets has become the main focus for astronomers and space agencies worldwide. With the launch of advanced satellites and exploration missions, scientists are able to detect potential habitats now beyond our solar system. The development of artificial intelligence and sophisticated navigation systems has made these missions more efficient. However, the challenge is still present such as the resources are limited and environmental conditions are difficult. If humans achieve self-sustaining colonies, __________''.
Students work individually or in pairs to complete the paragraph by emphasising creativity and using target vocabulary such as ''civilisation, exploration, radiation, vast, dynamic, potentially''. After completing their work they present their paragraphs to the class. The teacher checks and gives feedback on the use of language with target vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
SUPPORTING
Objective: To talk about possible future scenarios in space exploration in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing
The teacher shows some flashcards with visuals representing target vocabulary such as ''rocket, colony, AI, radiation, habitat'' and asks students to match the visuals with the correct words written on the board. When the matching activity is complete students work to complete a worksheet with target grammar in pairs. They use the matched vocabulary to fill in the blanks in sentences such as ''If humans colonise distant planets, civilisations will emerge there'' or ''If we explore the universe, we might discover unknown habitats''. The teacher checks and gives feedback on the use of language including target vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
